interests.title: Narcolepsy / EDS / wakefulness
interests.description: Deep clinical and mechanistic work on narcolepsy type 1 and 2, idiopathic hypersomnia, excessive daytime sleepiness and pathological hypoarousal. Especially interested in treatments that meaningfully change wakefulness, cognitive activation or functional capacity: orexin/hypocretin agonists, histamine/H3 mechanisms, pitolisant, modafinil/armodafinil, oxybates, stimulants, selegiline and MAO mechanisms, clarithromycin/flumazenil and GABA-A modulation, and unusual or neglected pharmacological approaches. Strong interest in actual magnitude of benefit, objective outcomes such as MWT/MSLT/PVT and real functional outcomes, not just questionnaire significance. Old or obscure studies are interesting if the signal is unusually strong. Also interested in pharmacology, dose-response, safety, drug interactions, biomarkers, pathophysiology, diagnostics beyond the MSLT and reasons promising treatments succeed or fail.
positive_signals: orexin/hypocretin agonist phase 2 or phase 3 results with actual numbers
large objective improvement in wakefulness, vigilance or functional capacity
head-to-head or unusually informative treatment comparisons
mechanistic explanation connecting pharmacology to wakefulness or hypoactivity
selegiline, MAO-B or monoaminergic wakefulness evidence
clarithromycin, flumazenil or GABA-A modulation in hypersomnolence
pitolisant, armodafinil, oxybate or stimulant comparative evidence
unexpected or overlooked older study with unusually strong results
dose-response, interaction or safety data that changes the practical picture
biomarkers or diagnostic advances beyond conventional MSLT interpretation
orexin biology or mechanisms of hypocretin neuron loss
negative_signals: basic explanation of what narcolepsy is
patient stories with no unusual clinical information
press releases that contain no useful numbers
small statistical effects presented as major clinical breakthroughs

interests.title: AI agents / coding / personal automation
interests.description: High-leverage developments in AI coding agents, Claude Code, Codex and similar systems, agent harnesses, context engineering, memory, MCP/tool use, browser automation, autonomous or semi-autonomous software engineering and personal automation. Especially interested in techniques or tools that let one person build substantially more, reduce supervision, preserve context across sessions, operate computers remotely or turn AI into persistent infrastructure rather than a chat interface. Also interested in clever lightweight implementations, open-source projects and unusual workflows involving terminals, mobile access, notifications and personal agents. Ignore routine AI product news unless it changes what is technically possible.
positive_signals: major Claude Code, Codex or coding-agent capability changes
agent architecture that materially improves reliability or autonomy
context compression, persistent memory or long-running agent techniques
novel MCP, tool-use, browser-control or computer-use implementations
strong coding-agent benchmarks with useful methodological details
small open-source project with disproportionately useful capabilities
personal AI infrastructure or automation that replaces substantial manual work
clever remote or mobile workflows for controlling development environments
evidence about what actually makes agents work better rather than prompt folklore
negative_signals: minor model releases with no practical consequence
benchmark announcements without enough information to interpret them

interests.title: Learning / memory / personal knowledge systems
interests.description: Research and systems for learning large conceptual domains efficiently with minimal cognitive overhead. Especially interested in understanding-first learning, retrieval practice, durable memory, semantic organization, compressed representations, hierarchical or graph-like knowledge structures, AI tutoring and using LLMs to convert large amounts of material or conversation history into compact usable memory. Interested in whether very lean representations can preserve enough structure for associative reconstruction, and in empirical comparisons of different learning strategies. Also interested in technical systems for conversation archives, semantic graphs, retrieval, RAG and long-term AI memory when they help construct a usable external mind.
positive_signals: controlled studies comparing learning or retrieval strategies
research on retrieval practice, spacing, memory consolidation or schema formation
minimal representations that produce surprisingly good recall
AI tutoring studies with measured learning outcomes
research on cognitive load and working-memory constraints
novel semantic memory, knowledge graph, RAG or long-term LLM memory architecture
conversation compression or personal knowledge systems that actually work at scale
evidence contradicting common study-method advice
negative_signals: claims about learning styles presented as established science

interests.title: Human interaction / attraction / behavioral psychology
interests.description: Technical, bottom-up work on real interpersonal behavior: attraction, flirting, interpersonal synchrony, mimicry, gaze, voice and prosody, approach and avoidance, status, dominance, submission, reinforcement, expectation, suggestibility, emotional contagion, group behavior, negotiation and relationship dynamics. Especially interested in research where small behavioral changes can be linked to subsequent changes in another person's behavior and where competing mechanisms can actually be distinguished. Prefer multimodal behavioral data, temporal sequences, experiments, longitudinal patterns, effect sizes and methodological criticism over broad psychological theories or self-help.
positive_signals: interpersonal synchrony or mimicry experiments
gaze, posture, distance, touch or vocal-prosody research
attraction or courtship studies with observable behavioral measures
temporal analysis showing one person's behavior predicting another's next response
status, dominance or submission studied behaviorally
suggestibility, reinforcement or conditioning inside social interaction
unexpected sex differences supported by strong data
high-resolution observational studies of real interaction
replications or failures that materially alter a familiar finding
cross-disciplinary work from ethology, linguistics, economics or neuroscience
negative_signals: pop psychology built around one famous experiment
claims that infer internal states from a single isolated gesture

interests.title: AI infrastructure / semis / Physical AI investing
interests.description: Investment-relevant developments where AI demand collides with physical bottlenecks: GPU infrastructure, datacenters, power, networking, optical interconnect and CPO, HBM and DRAM, foundry and packaging capacity, sensors, industrial automation, robotics and Physical AI. Particularly interested in underappreciated public companies or supply-chain nodes with asymmetric upside rather than already-consensus mega-cap AI exposure. Companies and themes of recurring interest include Nebius, VPG, COHR, LITE, TSEM, AAOI, IREN, APLD, CORZ, CIFR, Shunsin, memory/HBM and humanoid or industrial robotics. Focus on unit economics, capacity, contracts, bottlenecks, margins and evidence that expectations are materially wrong.
positive_signals: previously unknown capacity, contract or customer disclosure
supply bottleneck with identifiable beneficiaries
major change in HBM, DRAM, optics, CPO or AI networking economics
small or mid-cap company gaining structurally important AI exposure
management commentary containing concrete numbers
expert supply-chain evidence that contradicts consensus estimates
margin or utilization inflection with a clear mechanism
robotics or Physical AI development with investable upstream implications
primary-source filings, earnings calls and technical supplier disclosures
negative_signals: price targets without a model or argument
articles that mention AI without quantifying business exposure
mega-cap AI news with no implications for the relevant supply chain

interests.title: NBIS / Nebius
interests.description: Nebius Group as a business and investment: GPU capacity, datacenter construction, financing, utilization, cloud contracts, customer concentration, pricing and unit economics, ARR/revenue trajectory, margins and capital intensity, plus Avride, Toloka and TripleTen where material. Particularly interested in evidence that changes the long-term probability distribution rather than routine stock commentary, and in comparisons with CoreWeave, hyperscalers and other neoclouds. Large or unexplained stock moves are also relevant.
positive_signals: earnings, guidance, ARR and capacity disclosures
signed customer contracts and their economics
new datacenter or GPU capacity
financing or capex information that changes dilution or growth assumptions
utilization or margin evidence
major competitive development involving CoreWeave or hyperscalers
material Avride development
large or unexplained price movement
credible evidence that consensus expectations are substantially wrong
negative_signals: articles that repeat already-known company announcements

interests.title: EMDR / trauma processing mechanisms
interests.description: Deep mechanistic and clinical research on EMDR (Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing) and related bilateral/dual-attention trauma therapies. Especially interested in the actual proposed mechanisms of action (working memory taxation, orienting response, REM-sleep/thalamic-limbic analogues, interhemispheric interaction, adaptive information processing model) and the evidence for or against each; well-controlled dismantling studies isolating whether eye movements themselves add anything beyond exposure/reprocessing components; neuroimaging (fMRI/EEG/PET) findings during or after EMDR sessions; comparisons of EMDR against prolonged exposure, CPT, ketamine, MDMA-assisted therapy and other trauma treatments with real effect sizes and remission rates; and applications beyond classic PTSD (complex trauma, phobias, chronic pain, grief, psychosis-comorbid trauma). Also interested in critiques, replication failures, meta-analytic controversies, dose/protocol variations (movement speed, bilateral tactile/audio alternatives), and biomarkers predicting response.
positive_signals: dismantling or component-control studies isolating the eye-movement/bilateral-stimulation element
neuroimaging evidence of what EMDR changes in the brain during or after sessions
mechanistic theories tested against working-memory taxation or orienting-response accounts
head-to-head trials against prolonged exposure, CPT, MDMA- or ketamine-assisted therapy with real numbers
meta-analyses or replications that materially shift confidence in efficacy or mechanism
biomarkers or individual-difference predictors of EMDR response
protocol variation evidence: movement speed, bilateral audio/tactile alternatives, session dosing
applications to complex PTSD, phobias, chronic pain, grief or psychosis-comorbid trauma with objective outcomes
credible methodological critique or controversy in the EMDR efficacy literature
connections to sleep/REM physiology, memory reconsolidation or interhemispheric interaction research
negative_signals: basic explainer of what EMDR is or how a session works
patient testimonial with no clinical or mechanistic detail
small statistical effects presented as major breakthroughs

interests.title: Unexpected high-signal ideas
interests.description: Serendipity bucket for unusually interesting findings outside the predefined interests. Look for concrete, surprising and intellectually rich work in neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology, economics, biology, AI, social science, philosophy of mind or complex systems. The ideal item reveals a mechanism, experiment, dataset or phenomenon that is strange enough to provoke a long investigation or connects two domains in a non-obvious way. This is explicitly NOT a general science-news feed: ordinary important news is less interesting than a weird result with explanatory depth.
positive_signals: counterintuitive experimental result with strong evidence
weird behavioral or biological phenomenon with a plausible mechanism
cross-disciplinary result connecting previously separate ideas
new method that makes something previously difficult measurable
large replication that overturns conventional understanding
forgotten or obscure research that becomes newly relevant
specific phenomenon likely to generate several deeper questions
result where the details are substantially more interesting than the headline
negative_signals: interesting headline with no underlying mechanism or data
